questions.stem: A competitive inhibitor is added to an enzyme-controlled reaction. Which kinetic pattern is expected?
options: Higher apparent Km with unchanged Vmax
Unchanged Km with lower Vmax
Lower apparent Km and lower Vmax
Both Km and Vmax become zero
questions.explanation: More substrate is needed to reach half-maximal rate, so apparent Km rises. Sufficient substrate can outcompete the inhibitor, leaving Vmax unchanged.

questions.stem: Why can adding excess substrate fail to restore the original maximum rate in non-competitive inhibition?
options: The inhibitor permanently removes all substrate
The inhibitor reduces the amount of functional enzyme
The substrate stops colliding with enzymes
The active site becomes another substrate
questions.explanation: A pure non-competitive inhibitor reduces functional catalytic capacity through a separate binding site. More substrate cannot recover the lost Vmax.

questions.stem: An enzyme reaction slows sharply above its optimum temperature even though molecular collisions are more frequent. The best explanation is:
options: Substrate gains no kinetic energy
Activation energy increases because of more collisions
The enzyme's active-site shape is disrupted
All products become enzymes
questions.explanation: High temperature disrupts bonds maintaining tertiary structure. Loss of active-site complementarity outweighs the collision-rate increase.

questions.stem: A change in pH reduces enzyme activity without breaking peptide bonds. Which change most directly explains the result?
options: Loss of all water from the reaction
Removal of every carbon atom
Conversion of protein into DNA
Altered ionization of active-site groups
questions.explanation: pH changes the charge of amino-acid side chains, disturbing substrate binding or catalysis even when the primary structure remains intact.

questions.stem: An appropriate enzyme is added to a reaction mixture. Which outcome follows most directly?
options: The reaction reaches equilibrium faster
An enzyme-substrate complex forms readily
The same enzyme molecule can catalyse another reaction
The initial reaction rate increases
questions.explanation: The reaction reaches equilibrium faster. The enzyme provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy.
